unmapped_findings: The volume fraction of Fe3AlC0.5 precipitates increases significantly with increasing carbon content, being highest in Fe-7Al-1.0C (b0061, figure_005).

The room-temperature ductility decrease with increasing carbon is attributed solely to the increase in the volume fraction of hard and brittle Fe3AlC0.5 precipitates; Fe-7Al alloys are not susceptible to environmental embrittlement (b0062).

Table V and Fig. 5 captions for the carbon-series alloys label the melting route 'AIM', while the section text (b0060) states the alloys were prepared by air induction melting with a flux cover (AIMFC).
